title: Integer richness assumptions gave lower evenness in six California pollution comparisons from 2001-2002
abstract: We tested whether paired richness and Shannon summaries fix the direction of mean log Hill evenness under pollution. A 2024 public workbook supplied nine paired comparisons from two papers. Under positive integer richness counts, reported sample standard deviations and natural logarithm entropy, all six California host-year contrasts were negative at a summary tolerance of 0.005. Each arm allowed one sorted count triple. A UK ozone pair gave a positive relaxed moment bound. Two other UK pairs could not fit the integer model at their stated sample size and this tolerance. With no integer or variance constraint, all nine conservative bounds included zero. These are conditional possibility bounds, not confidence intervals. Shared sites, selected reports, unknown sampling coverage and unverified endpoint alignment limit inference. The evidence does not show a common pollutant effect, a climate interaction or causal biodiversity loss. Code, source hashes, aggregate bounds and a figure are included; source records remain external.

display.caption: Conditional contrast bounds at summary tolerance 0.005. The integer model is not feasible for two omitted UK comparisons. Lines are possibility bounds, not sampling intervals. Orange points use logarithms of mean richness.
